findings.reason: a node building to the gate as written puts the refusal in the per-candidate check and then cannot satisfy the gate for an exhausted dropped-edge name, or satisfies the gate and leaves §37's actual gap open.
findings.text: the gate `g-s38-needs-source-audit` measures "the export refuses a planted dropped-edge name ... through `_has_producing_source`", but §37 (plan.html:245) states the export refuses "before building its population while the function reports any dropped or never-bound live name" and that "`_has_producing_source` stays the per-candidate eligibility check" — the two name opposite refusal sites, and the one the gate names cannot reach the names §37 exists to catch, because `_fetch_export_population` (export.py:611) admits only `accepted`/`approved` so the 240 exhausted names never reach the per-candidate check at all

findings.reason: the section states one definition of "sourced" and the census it delegates to uses another, so a node following the stated reuse returns nothing for the planted parent and fails its own first measure. Today the parent passes the export through `_has_live_child` and would call it a defect; a node following §37 literally would call it fine; the plan should say which applies and name the precedence, since the plan is the semantic authority for the classifier's definition.
findings.text: §37 says the classifier "reuses the child-evidence rule `_has_producing_source` applies, so there is one definition of 'sourced'", but under that rule (`_has_producing_source`'s `_has_live_child`, export.py:795-810) a derived parent with a live child is sourced and so would not be a "sourceless name" the function returns a population for, while §35 defines population 1 as exactly that parent ("`origin = derived` with children. They legitimately have no source") and §37's done-when requires "the function places each in its population" for a fixture that plants that parent
